Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# oha (おはよう)

[![GitHub Actions](https://github.com/hatoo/oha/workflows/CI/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hatoo/oha/actions?query=workflow%3ACI)
[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/oha.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/oha)
[![Arch Linux](https://img.shields.io/archlinux/v/extra/x86_64/oha)](https://archlinux.org/packages/extra/x86_64/oha/)
[![Homebrew](https://img.shields.io/homebrew/v/oha)](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/oha)

[![ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/img/githubbutton_sm.svg)](https://ko-fi.com/hatoo)

oha is a tiny program that sends some load to a web application and show realtime tui inspired by [rakyll/hey](https://github.com/rakyll/hey).

This program is written in Rust and powered by [tokio](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio) and beautiful tui by [ratatui](https://github.com/ratatui-org/ratatui).

![demo](demo.gif)

# Installation

This program is built on stable Rust, with both `make` and `cmake` prerequisites to install via cargo.

    cargo install oha

You can optionally build oha against [native-tls](https://github.com/sfackler/rust-native-tls) instead of [rustls](https://github.com/rustls/rustls).

    cargo install --no-default-features --features native-tls oha

You can enable VSOCK support by enabling `vsock` feature.

    cargo install --features vsock oha

You can enable experimental HTTP3 support by enabling the `http3` feature. This uses the [H3](https://github.com/hyperium/h3/r) library by the developers of Hyper.
It will remain experimental as long as H3 is experimental. It currently depends on using `rustls` for TLS.

## Download pre-built binary

You can download pre-built binary from [Release page](https://github.com/hatoo/oha/releases) for each version and from [Publish workflow](https://github.com/hatoo/oha/actions/workflows/release.yml) and [Publish PGO workflow](https://github.com/hatoo/oha/actions/workflows/release-pgo.yml) for each commit.

## On Arch Linux

    pacman -S oha

## On macOS (Homebrew)

    brew install oha

## On Windows (winget)

    winget install hatoo.oha

## On Debian ([Azlux's repository](http://packages.azlux.fr/))

    echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/azlux-archive-keyring.gpg] http://packages.azlux.fr/debian/ stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/azlux.list
    sudo wget -O /usr/share/keyrings/azlux-archive-keyring.gpg https://azlux.fr/repo.gpg
    apt update
    apt install oha

## X-CMD (Linux, macOS, Windows WSL/GitBash)

You can install with [x-cmd](https://www.x-cmd.com).

```sh
x env use oha
```

## Containerized

### Official Docker image

[ghcr.io/hatoo/oha](https://github.com/hatoo/oha/pkgs/container/oha)

### Build image locally

You can also build and create a container image including oha

```sh
docker build -t hatoo/oha:latest .
```

Then you can use oha directly through the container

```sh
docker run --rm -it --network=host hatoo/oha:latest https://example.com:3000
```

## Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO)

You can build `oha` with PGO by using the following commands:

```sh
bun run pgo.js
```

And the binary will be available at `target/[target-triple]/pgo/oha`.

**Note**: Please keep in mind that in order to run the aforementioned command,
you need to have installed `cargo-pgo` cargo package.

You can install it via `cargo install cargo-pgo`.

# Platform

- Linux - Tested on Ubuntu 18.04 gnome-terminal
- Windows 10 - Tested on Windows Powershell
- MacOS - Tested on iTerm2

# Performance

`oha` uses faster implementation when `--no-tui` option is set and both `-q` and `--burst-delay` are not set because it can avoid overhead to gather data realtime.

# Output

By default `oha` outputs a text summary of the results.

`oha` prints JSON summary output when `--output-format json` option is set.
The schema of JSON output is defined in [schema.json](./schema.json).

When `--output-format csv` is used result of each request is printed as a line of comma separated values.

# Tips

## Stress test in more realistic condition

`oha` uses default options inherited from [rakyll/hey](https://github.com/rakyll/hey) but you may need to change options to stress test in more realistic condition.

I suggest to run `oha` with following options.

```sh
oha <-z or -n> -c <number of concurrent connections> -q <query per seconds> --latency-correction --disable-keepalive <target-address>
```

- --disable-keepalive

    In real, user doesn't query same URL using [Keep-Alive](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Keep-Alive). You may want to run without `Keep-Alive`.
- --latency-correction

    You can avoid `Coordinated Omission Problem` by using `--latency-correction`.

## Burst feature

You can use `--burst-delay` along with `--burst-rate` option to introduce delay between a defined number of requests.

```sh
oha -n 10 --burst-delay 2s --burst-rate 4
```

In this particular scenario, every 2 seconds, 4 requests will be processed, and after 6s the total of 10 requests will be processed.
*NOTE: If you don't set `--burst-rate` option, the amount is default to 1*

## Dynamic url feature

You can use `--rand-regex-url` option to generate random url for each connection.

```sh
oha --rand-regex-url http://127.0.0.1/[a-z][a-z][0-9]
```

Each Urls are generated by [rand_regex](https://github.com/kennytm/rand_regex) crate but regex's dot is disabled since it's not useful for this purpose and it's very inconvenient if url's dots are interpreted as regex's dot.

Optionally you can set `--max-repeat` option to limit max repeat count for each regex. e.g http://127.0.0.1/[a-z]* with `--max-repeat 4` will generate url like http://127.0.0.1/[a-z]{0,4}

Currently dynamic scheme, host and port with keep-alive are not works well.

## URLs from file feature

You can use `--urls-from-file` to read the target URLs from a file. Each line of this file needs to contain one valid URL as in the example below.

```
http://domain.tld/foo/bar

# Performance

`oha` uses faster implementation when `--no-tui` option is set and both `-q` and `--burst-delay` are not set because it can avoid overhead to gather data realtime.

# Output

By default `oha` outputs a text summary of the results.

`oha` prints JSON summary output when `--output-format json` option is set.
The schema of JSON output is defined in [schema.json](./schema.json).

When `--output-format csv` is used result of each request is printed as a line of comma separated values.

# Tips

## Stress test in more realistic condition

`oha` uses default options inherited from [rakyll/hey](https://github.com/rakyll/hey) but you may need to change options to stress test in more realistic condition.

I suggest to run `oha` with following options.

```sh
oha <-z or -n> -c <number of concurrent connections> -q <query per seconds> --latency-correction --disable-keepalive <target-address>
```

- --disable-keepalive

    In real, user doesn't query same URL using [Keep-Alive](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Keep-Alive). You may want to run without `Keep-Alive`.
- --latency-correction

    You can avoid `Coordinated Omission Problem` by using `--latency-correction`.

## Burst feature

You can use `--burst-delay` along with `--burst-rate` option to introduce delay between a defined number of requests.

```sh
oha -n 10 --burst-delay 2s --burst-rate 4
```

In this particular scenario, every 2 seconds, 4 requests will be processed, and after 6s the total of 10 requests will be processed.
*NOTE: If you don't set `--burst-rate` option, the amount is default to 1*

cat >> implementation/stats.py <<'PY'


def colorize_report(text, statistics):
    import re
    def color(s, n, bold=False):
        return f'\x1b[38;5;{n}m' + ('\x1b[1m' if bold else '') + s + ('\x1b[0m' if bold else '\x1b[39m')
    def time_color(line):
        m = re.search(r'(NaN|[0-9.]+) (ns|us|ms|sec|min|hr)', line)
        if not m or m[1] == 'NaN': return 9
        factor = {'ns':1e-9,'us':1e-6,'ms':.001,'sec':1,'min':60,'hr':3600}[m[2]]
        t = float(m[1])*factor
        return 10 if t < .1 else 11 if t < .5 else 9
    result = []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if line and not line.startswith(' '):
            line = '\x1b[1m\x1b[4m' + line + '\x1b[0m'
        elif line.startswith('  Success rate:'):
            line = color(line, 10 if statistics.success == 1 else 11 if statistics.success >= .99 else 9, True)
        elif line.startswith('  Slowest:'): line = color(line,11)
        elif line.startswith('  Fastest:'): line = color(line,10)
        elif line.startswith('  Average:'): line = color(line,14)
        elif '[' in line and '|' in line:
            first, bars = line.split('|',1)
            c = time_color(line)
            line = color(first+'|',c)+''.join(color(ch,c) for ch in bars)
        elif re.match(r'  [0-9.]+% in ',line): line = color(line,time_color(line))
        elif re.match(r'  \[\d+\] \d+ responses',line):
            status = int(line.split('[',1)[1].split(']',1)[0])
            line = color(line,10 if 200 <= status < 300 else 11 if 300 <= status < 400 else 9)
        elif re.match(r'  \[\d+\] ',line): line = color(line,9)
        result.append(line)
    return '\n'.join(result)+'\n'

        env = os.environ.copy()
        env.pop('NO_COLOR', None)
        return subprocess.run([str(BINARY), *args], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                              env=env, timeout=timeout)

    def report(self, *args, path='/'):
        result = self.run_cli('--no-tui', '--output-format', 'json', *args, self.url+path)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr, b'')
        return json.loads(result.stdout)

    def test_help_and_version(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli('--version').stdout, b'oha 1.12.1\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli('-h').stdout, self.run_cli('--help').stdout)
        self.assertIn(b'--output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>', self.run_cli('--help').stdout)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli().returncode, 2)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli().stderr, self.run_cli('--help').stdout)

    def test_numeric_parsers_and_duration_errors(self):
        for args in [('-n', '1.5k'), ('-n', '2M'), ('-z', '1h30m'), ('-n', '+2')]:
            result = self.run_cli(*args, '--dump-urls', '0', self.url)
            self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        result = self.run_cli('-n', 'abc', self.url)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2)
        self.assertIn(b"invalid value 'abc' for '-n <N_REQUESTS>': invalid digit found in string", result.stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'time unit needed, for example 10sec or 10ms', self.run_cli('-z', '10', self.url).stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'cannot be used', self.run_cli('-n','1','-z','1s',self.url).stderr)

    def test_requirements_and_conflicts(self):
        for args, missing in [(('--cert','abc'), b'--key <KEY>'),
                              (('--burst-delay','1s'), b'--burst-rate <BURST_REQUESTS>'),
                              (('--max-repeat','2'), b'--rand-regex-url')]:
            result = self.run_cli(*args, self.url)
            self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2)
            self.assertIn(missing, result.stderr)
        result = self.run_cli('-d','a','-D','b',self.url)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2)
        self.assertIn(b"'-d <BODY_STRING>' cannot be used with '-D <BODY_PATH>'", result.stderr)

    def test_url_normalization(self):
        cases = {
            'HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM:80/a/../b?q=hello world#x': 'http://example.com/b?q=hello%20world#x',
            'http://127.1': 'http://127.0.0.1/',
            'http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]': 'http://[::ffff:7f00:1]/',
            'https://bücher.example': 'https://xn--bcher-kva.example/',
        }
        for value, normalized in cases.items():
            result = self.run_cli('--dump-urls','2',value)
            self.assertEqual(result.stdout.decode(), (normalized+'\n')*2)
            self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli('--dump-urls','1','foo').stderr, b'Error: relative URL without a base\n')

    def test_random_urls(self):
        result = self.run_cli('--rand-regex-url', '--dump-urls', '20', 'http://localhost/[a-c]{3}/[0-9]{2}')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        for line in result.stdout.decode().splitlines():
            self.assertRegex(line, r'^http://localhost/[abc]{3}/[0-9]{2}$')
        result = self.run_cli('--rand-regex-url','--dump-urls','1','http://localhost/[')
        self.assertIn(b'error: unclosed character class', result.stderr)

    def test_debug_request_and_headers(self):
        result = self.run_cli('--debug', '-m','POST', '-d','abc', '-a','u:p', '-H','X-Test: first', '-H','x-test: second', self.url+'/body')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        output = result.stdout.decode()
        self.assertIn('    method: POST,\n', output)
        self.assertIn('"authorization": "Basic dTpw",', output)
        self.assertIn('"x-test": "second",', output)
        self.assertIn('            b"abc",', output)
        self.assertIn('    body: b"abc",', output)
        self.assertNotIn('Summary:', output)

    def test_json_success_and_http_error_status(self):
        for path, status in [('/',200),('/status/404',404),('/status/500',500)]:
            result = self.report('-n','4','-c','2',path=path)
            self.assertEqual(result['summary']['totalData'], 20)
            self.assertEqual(result['summary']['sizePerRequest'], 5)
            self.assertEqual(result['summary']['successRate'], 1.0)
            self.assertEqual(result['statusCodeDistribution'], {str(status):4})
            self.assertEqual(result['errorDistribution'], {})
            self.assertGreater(result['summary']['total'], 0)

    def test_redirect_and_head(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.report('-n','1','-c','1',path='/redirect')['statusCodeDistribution'], {'200':1})
        self.assertEqual(self.report('-n','1','-c','1','-r','0',path='/redirect')['statusCodeDistribution'], {'302':1})
        self.assertEqual(self.report('-n','2','-c','1','-m','HEAD')['summary']['totalData'], 0)
        self.assertIn('    status: 302,', self.run_cli('--debug',self.url+'/redirect').stdout.decode())

    def test_timeouts_and_empty_reports(self):
        result = self.report('-n','2','-c','1','-t','10ms',path='/slow')
        self.assertEqual(result['errorDistribution'], {'timeout':2})
        self.assertEqual(result['summary']['successRate'], 0.0)
        self.assertIsNone(result['summary']['average'])
        result = self.report('-n','0')
        self.assertIsNone(result['summary']['successRate'])
        self.assertEqual(result['responseTimeHistogram'], {'NaN':0})
        self.assertEqual(result['statusCodeDistribution'], {})
        result = self.report('-n','2','-c','1','--stats-success-breakdown')
        self.assertEqual(result['responseTimeHistogramNotSuccessful'], {'NaN':0})

    def test_deadline(self):
        result = self.report('-z','25ms','-c','1',path='/slow')
        self.assertEqual(result['errorDistribution'], {'aborted due to deadline':1})
        self.assertIsNone(result['summary']['successRate'])

    def test_csv_and_quiet(self):
        result = self.run_cli('--no-tui','--output-format','csv','-n','3','-c','1',self.url+'/')
        lines = result.stdout.decode().splitlines()
        self.assertEqual(lines[0], 'request-start,DNS,DNS+dialup,Response-delay,request-duration,bytes,status')
        self.assertEqual(len(lines), 4)
        for line in lines[1:]: self.assertTrue(line.endswith(',5,200'))
        result = self.run_cli('--no-tui','--output-format','quiet','-n','2',self.url+'/')
        self.assertEqual((result.returncode,result.stdout,result.stderr),(0,b'',b''))

    def test_files_and_database(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            d = pathlib.Path(d)
            urls, body, out, db = (d/x for x in ('urls','body','out','run.db'))
            urls.write_text(self.url+'/\n\n'+self.url+'/status/404\n')
            result = self.run_cli('--urls-from-file','--dump-urls','8',str(urls))
            self.assertEqual(result.returncode,0)
            self.assertTrue(set(result.stdout.decode().splitlines()).issubset({self.url+'/',self.url+'/status/404'}))
            body.write_bytes(b'payload')
            result = self.run_cli('--no-tui','--output-format','json','-n','2','-c','1','-D',str(body),'-o',str(out),'--db-url',str(db),self.url+'/body')
            self.assertEqual(result.returncode,0,result.stderr)
            self.assertEqual(result.stdout,b'')
            report = json.loads(out.read_text())
            self.assertEqual(report['summary']['totalData'],14)
            con = sqlite3.connect(db)
            rows = con.execute('select url,status,len_bytes from oha').fetchall()
            con.close()
            self.assertEqual(rows,[('/body',200,7)]*2)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

# Independent implementation

The command is implemented in Python, using only the standard library. Build it
with `./compile.sh`. This creates a self-contained executable Python archive at
`./executable`; it does not need the source directory at runtime.

Run the regression suite after building:

```
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The implementation separates command-line validation, URL generation, HTTP
transport, scheduling, and report generation. HTTP/1 requests are written and
parsed directly over sockets. TLS uses the standard SSL module. HTTP/2 framing
and header compression are implemented separately; the prefix-code data was
measured from request traffic produced during local CLI experiments. SQLite
output uses the standard database module.

Some observed details deliberately differ from the prose documentation:

- Request-count and duration options conflict. Burst delay/rate require one
  another, and an explicit maximum repetition count requires regex URL mode.
- Debug mode makes one request, without following redirects or imposing the
  per-request timeout. URL dumping exits before request-body preparation.
- HTTP error responses are completed requests, not transport failures. Deadline
  cancellation is excluded from the success-rate denominator.
- The explicit latency-correction flag suppresses the queued-start timestamp;
  rate-limited runs without that flag include it.
- Reports retain the observed empty-distribution and single-sample conventions.

Generated archives, caches, databases, logs, and build directories are ignored
by Git. The bundled README and license are preserved as supplied documentation.

import math
import pathlib
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'implementation'))
from stats import histogram, hist_map, percentiles, rps_values, Statistics
from http2 import Decoder, encode
import huffman


class ReportTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_single_and_empty_histograms(self):
        self.assertEqual(hist_map([.25]), {'0.25':0})
        self.assertEqual(histogram([.25])[0], (.25,1))
        self.assertEqual(hist_map([]), {'NaN':0})

    def test_percentile_selection(self):
        p = percentiles([2.,1.])
        self.assertEqual(p['p25'],1.)
        self.assertEqual(p['p50'],2.)
        self.assertTrue(math.isnan(percentiles([])['p99']))

    def test_rps_windows(self):
        times = [.002747641,.003118742,.004026407,.004527711,.005261775,.043456403,
                 .044380982,.045242843,.045395821,.046702274]
        values = rps_values([{'end':t} for t in times])
        self.assertEqual(len(values),3)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(values[0],5/.005261775)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(values[1],1/(.043456403-.005261775))
        self.assertAlmostEqual(values[2],4/(.046702274-.043456403))

    def test_deadline_denominator(self):
        s = Statistics([], {'aborted due to deadline':2}, .1)
        self.assertTrue(math.isnan(s.success))
        self.assertEqual(s.rps,20.)

    def test_hpack_and_huffman(self):
        fields = [(b':status',b'200'),(b'content-length',b'5'),(b'x-test',b'hello')]
        self.assertEqual(Decoder().decode(encode(fields)),fields)
        self.assertEqual(huffman.decode(bytes.fromhex('18c6318c63')),b'aaaaaaaa')
        self.assertEqual(huffman.decode(bytes.fromhex('f2b5761e32ff')),b'x-probe')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

import math
import pathlib
import sys
import unittest

sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'implementation'))
from stats import histogram, hist_map, percentiles, rps_values, Statistics
from http2 import Decoder, encode
import huffman


class ReportTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_single_and_empty_histograms(self):
        self.assertEqual(hist_map([.25]), {'0.25':0})
        self.assertEqual(histogram([.25])[0], (.25,1))
        self.assertEqual(hist_map([]), {'NaN':0})

    def test_percentile_selection(self):
        p = percentiles([2.,1.])
        self.assertEqual(p['p25'],1.)
        self.assertEqual(p['p50'],2.)
        self.assertTrue(math.isnan(percentiles([])['p99']))

    def test_rps_windows(self):
        times = [.002747641,.003118742,.004026407,.004527711,.005261775,.043456403,
                 .044380982,.045242843,.045395821,.046702274]
        values = rps_values([{'end':t} for t in times])
        self.assertEqual(len(values),3)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(values[0],5/.005261775)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(values[1],1/(.043456403-.005261775))
        self.assertAlmostEqual(values[2],4/(.046702274-.043456403))

    def test_deadline_denominator(self):
        s = Statistics([], {'aborted due to deadline':2}, .1)
        self.assertTrue(math.isnan(s.success))
        self.assertEqual(s.rps,20.)

    def test_hpack_and_huffman(self):
        fields = [(b':status',b'200'),(b'content-length',b'5'),(b'x-test',b'hello')]
        self.assertEqual(Decoder().decode(encode(fields)),fields)
        self.assertEqual(huffman.decode(bytes.fromhex('18c6318c63')),b'aaaaaaaa')
        self.assertEqual(huffman.decode(bytes.fromhex('f2b5761e32ff')),b'x-probe')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
